headline: Habagat Brings Heavy Rain Risk to Zambales as PAGASA Warns of Floods and Landslides
seoTitle: Habagat Heavy Rain Risk in Zambales Aug. 28 | FMB News
seoDescription: PAGASA forecasts persistent Habagat rains over Zambales and nearby western Luzon areas on August 28, with flood and landslide risks in saturated communities.
deck: Western Luzon faces another wet Friday as the southwest monsoon continues to feed rain into Zambales and nearby provinces, with local class suspensions reported in affected communities.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: PAGASA continued to flag heavy-rain risk over western Luzon heading into Friday, August 28, as the Southwest Monsoon or Habagat remained active. The approved FMB News overnight brief reported an Orange-level rainfall warning for Zambales, with other western and northern Luzon areas under lower-level advisories.
The same newsroom brief reported localized class suspensions in parts of Zambales and Bataan as local governments shifted affected learners away from in-person classes.

sections.heading: What PAGASA shows
paragraphs: PAGASA's official outlook for August 26 to 28 calls for occasional rains over Zambales, Bataan and Occidental Mindoro due to Habagat. Its selected-city outlook shows Olongapo/SBMA under occasional rains on Friday and monsoon rains over the weekend.

A PAGASA Northern Luzon rainfall advisory issued at 2:00 AM on August 28 also warned of light to moderate to at times heavy rains in parts of Pangasinan, Batanes, Abra, Ilocos Sur, Benguet, Nueva Vizcaya and La Union, with landslide, mudslide, rockslide and flash-flood precautions advised.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Soils across parts of western Luzon have already absorbed repeated rounds of rain. That raises the risk that additional rainfall can trigger localized flooding or slope failures even when rainfall intensity varies from one municipality to another.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Residents in flood-prone and landslide-prone communities should follow the latest PAGASA rainfall warnings and local disaster-office instructions because warning levels and affected municipalities can change quickly.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: PAGASA forecasts continued wet conditions in Olongapo and western Luzon through the weekend. Updated rainfall warnings, river-basin advisories and local class or work suspensions should be treated as the controlling information for each locality.
